subject: Proposal workflow idea for Persistent Systems
email:
Hi Persistent Systems team,

I was looking through Persistent Systems' public site and noticed public positioning across digital engineering, banking, cloud transformation.

That made me curious about the document work behind those opportunities. For complex regulated-industry engagements, proposal teams may need to adapt technical scope, proof points, delivery language, and reusable case-study material for each opportunity.

One SuperDocs workflow I would test is starting from an approved proposal or RFP document, updating only the relevant sections for the opportunity, and leaving the result in the document for human review rather than producing disconnected copy in a chat window.

I would want to validate whether that is actually a painful part of your workflow before assuming the fit.

Best,
Growth Machine Demo
follow_up: Following up on the document-workflow idea for Persistent Systems. The hypothesis I would want to validate is simple: For complex regulated-industry engagements, proposal teams may need to adapt technical scope, proof points, delivery language, and reusable case-study material for each opportunity. The goal would be to reduce repetitive editing without removing proposal-owner review.
